title: Filling the Ward 10 council vacancy
subtitle: Expanded administrative penalties for non-parking bylaw offences and appointment of AMPS hearing officers.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended filling the vacant Ward 10 council seat by appointing the runner-up from the 2022 municipal election, rather than holding a by-election {{vote:m2}}. The City Clerk would confirm the candidate's qualifications and consent, and an appointment by-law would go to the next Council meeting. Supporters pointed to the close 2022 result, the cost of a by-election and the length of time the ward has been without a councillor. Others argued a by-election is the more democratic route with almost three years left in the term.

The committee also recommended moving 25 non-parking bylaws, including noise, graffiti, signs, and snow and ice removal, from the provincial court system to the City's Administrative Monetary Penalty System (AMPS) {{vote:m3}}. Staff said this would give residents 30 days to respond, an internal screening and hearing process, and shorter waits than the current six to eight months for a court trial. Staff expect a go-live in May or June 2024.

The committee further recommended appointing five AMPS hearing officers through December 2026 and keeping the current per diem honorarium {{vote:m1}}. All three items go to a Special Council meeting later the same day.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended filling the Ward 10 vacancy by appointing the 2022 election runner-up, Stephanie Stretch, and directed the Clerk to confirm qualifications and consent and bring forward an appointment by-law.

The committee recommended moving non-parking bylaw offences into the Administrative Monetary Penalty System, with a new Administrative Penalty By-law, a repeal and replacement of the Screening and Hearing Officer By-law, and amendments to 25 bylaw chapters and six policies.

The committee recommended appointing five hearing officers for a term ending December 2026, keeping the per diem honorarium of $260 per half day and $520 per full day, and indemnifying them under the City's by-law.
The committee recommended delegating authority to the City Clerk to sign agreements with the hearing officers on terms satisfactory to the City Solicitor.

debate: Supporters of appointing the runner-up said the 2022 result was very close, the top two candidates had similar platforms, and the runner-up won half the polling stations. They also cited the cost of a by-election (staff estimated roughly $77,000 to $100,000, not counting some staffing and advertising costs) and the need for a downtown representative sooner.

Councillors favouring a by-election said democracy is worth the cost, that nearly three years remain in the term, and that voters should choose. They noted candidates and circumstances may have changed since 2022, and said low turnout is not a reason to skip an election.

Delegates were split. One supported appointing the runner-up, citing the similar platforms and the risk of low by-election turnout. One proposed a randomly selected citizens' assembly of Ward 10 voters. Another favoured a by-election to give the new councillor a mandate, and urged better voter information. Staff said the assembly idea was new to them and would be hard to fit in the 60-day deadline.

On AMPS, councillors asked about financial hardship and the late and collection fees. Staff said hardship and extenuating circumstances can be considered in the dispute process. They also said the snow-removal chapter's missing penalty amount was an error that would be fixed before Council.
